Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

The game works, and now we want prizes.

The quiz settings get a new field, "Number of winners" (a number, at least 1, 3 by default).

Scoring:

- Each correct answer gives one point.
- Players with equal points are ranked by speed: the total time of their correct answers wins when it is lower. The time of an answer runs from the moment the question opens to the player's last pick.
- Players don't see points during the game.

Speed now decides ties, so all players must get each question at the same moment: the big screen and the phones must follow the moderator close to instantly.

After "End quiz":

- The big screen shows the leaderboard: one list item for each player, in order, with the place, the name, and the points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points").
- Each player's phone shows the place ("Place 2 of 5") and the points ("3 points").

Picking the winners (N is the number of winners):

- The "Top N" button (for example, "Top 3") makes the first N players of the leaderboard the winners.
- The "Draw" button is for ties. Every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points (speed doesn't matter here). Each click draws again.
- Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
- The "Reset winners" button removes the winners.
- Winners get the "Winner" mark on the leaderboard, and their phones show "You won!". Both update live.

# Quizzy

A live quiz app for conference talks. The moderator prepares quizzes under
`/moderate`, starts a game for a quiz, and shows the big screen. The audience joins
on their phones with a link or QR code, answers the questions live, and sees the
results. Quizzes can be exported and imported as JSON.

## Run it

    RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 \
    SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
    QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... \
    bin/serve

`bin/serve` prepares the database and assets and runs the app in the foreground.
All data is kept under `storage/`. `GET /up` answers 200 when the app is ready.

    bin/rails test          # models and integration tests
    bin/rails test:system   # browser tests (Chromium, via Cuprite), including live games

`bin/rails test:system` starts several browser sessions: the big screen and phones.

# Quizzy: design notes

Notes for whoever builds the next release. The live game (big screen, phones) is in "Live game".
The design files live in `docs/mockups/` (style guide, quiz page, question form).

## Running it

    RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
    QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... bin/serve

`bin/serve` creates or migrates the SQLite databases (`db:prepare`), precompiles
assets (`assets:precompile`, digests into `public/assets`), and then runs Puma in
the foreground on `0.0.0.0:$PORT`. It exits with an error if one of the three
required variables is missing.

- All data lives in `storage/`: `production.sqlite3` (quizzes), `production_cache`,
  `production_queue` and `production_cable` (Solid Cache/Queue/Cable, unused so far).
- Logs go to STDOUT (default production logging). Nothing calls external services.
- Plain HTTP, no `force_ssl`, no host allow-list (`config.hosts` is empty in production).
- `GET /up` returns 200 without credentials.

## Routes and access

Everything under `/moderate` goes through `Moderate::BaseController`, which runs
HTTP Basic auth first. Unset, wrong, or empty credentials give 401 with
`WWW-Authenticate`. Unknown `/moderate/*` URLs also ask for credentials before
returning 404, so the route table does not leak to anonymous visitors.
The comparison uses `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.

| Page | Route |
| --- | --- |
| Quiz list, "New quiz" | `GET /moderate` (`moderate_root`) |
| New quiz / save | `GET /moderate/quizzes/new`, `POST /moderate/quizzes` |
| Quiz page | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id` |
| Settings (quiz form) and "Delete quiz" | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/edit`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /moderate/quizzes/:id` |
| Preview | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/preview` |
| Export (quiz as JSON in a `<pre>`) | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` |
| Import page / import (always a new quiz) | `GET /moderate/imports/new`, `POST /moderate/imports` |
| New / edit question | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/new`, `…/:id/edit` |
| Save question, delete | `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions[/:id]` |
| Move up / down | `POST /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/:id/move?direction=up|down` |
| Active checkbox | `PATCH /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/:id/activation` |

## Data model

- `Quiz`: `title` (required).
- `Question`: `quiz_id`, `text` (required), `position` (1-based, per quiz), `active`
  (default true). Inactive questions stay in the order. Numbering on the quiz page
  ("1", "2", …) counts active questions only; inactive ones show "—".
- `Option`: `question_id`, `text`, `correct`, `position`.

### Option rules (`Question`)

- Rows whose text is blank after `strip` are skipped and never saved.
- At least two filled rows: otherwise "Add at least two options".
- At least one filled row must be correct (several correct rows are fine). A
  correct box on an empty row does not count. Otherwise "Mark at least one option
  as correct".
- Validation runs on the in-memory rows. Options are only replaced after validation
  passes (`after_save`), so a ",

`GameScreen#option_rows` and `PlayerScreen#option_rows` give `correct` as `nil` while the
question is open, so the markup has no way to show it. The open-question phone page
contains no "correct" text at all (checked by `test/integration/play_test.rb`, and by a
check against the production server). Signals carry no game data, so a broadcast
cannot leak either.

Phones show the result after Finish: "Correct!", "Wrong!" or "No answer", with the right

### Live updates

- **Push**: every state change and every answer sends a short Turbo Stream
  `live_refresh` signal, with no data, to two signed streams: `[game, :screen]` (the big
  screen) and `[game, :players]` (all phones). The signal is sent after the transaction
  commits.
- **Pull**: the `live` Stimulus controller (`app/javascript/controllers/live_controller.js`)
  owns one region (`#game-screen` or `#player-screen`). On a signal, or on its timer, it
  fetches the region's HTML and swaps it in if the `data-live-version-value` changed.
  Each phone fetches its own state with its cookie, so no one sees another player's pick.
  The server answers `304` when the version has not changed (ETag).
- **Fallback**: the timer (about 3 s for the big screen, 5 s for phones, with jitter) and
  the `visibilitychange` and `online` events make a region catch up when a socket drops
  or a signal is lost. This is what copes with crowded conference Wi-Fi. Tests in
  `test/system/live_fallback_browser_test.rb` mute the push and check the timers.
- **Failed taps**: Turbo's `turbo:fetch-request-error` on a live region adds "No connection.
  Nothing was sent. Try again." The button dims while the request is in flight (`aria-busy`).
- The join form is only replaced when the quiz ends, so a name being typed is not lost.
- The custom stream action `live_refresh` is defined in `app/javascript/application.js`.

### Gotchas

- Propshaft reads `public/assets/.manifest.json` when it exists, even in test. A stale
  `public/assets` (left behind by an earlier `bin/serve`) makes the test server load an old
  `application.js`. Delete `public/assets` after a manual build, or run `bin/serve` again.
  It is gitignored.
- Turbo's broadcast assertions are not loaded into `ActiveSupport::TestCase` by default.
  `test_helper.rb` includes `Turbo::Broadcastable::TestHelper`. Use
  `assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts ..., count: 0` to assert that nothing was sent.
- A flex container splits its children into separate lines in the browser's text. A
  label and a number in separate elements inside `.counter-pill` read "Players:" and "2"
  on separate lines. Keep the label and the number in one inline element (see the
  `counter-pill` in `app/views/moderate/games/_screen.html.erb`).
- The row objects for the screens (`GameScreen::Row`, `PlayerScreen::Row`) are built
  with `correct` set to `nil` until it is revealed, so a partial cannot print a flag
  that was never revealed.

### Decisions

- A game copies the quiz when it starts, not when it is created. The lobby can wait for
  players while the moderator fixes a typo in a question. "Start a game" refuses when
  the quiz has no active question, and so does Start, with a message.
- "Players" means everyone who joined the game. Nobody can leave or be removed, so
  the answer counter's denominator is the number of joined players. Players who join
  after the start count too.
- The join link on the big screen is built from the request host
  (`http://host:port/play/CODE`). Open the big screen through an address the phones can
  reach, for example the LAN address.
- The phone's player is kept in a signed, permanent cookie named after the code
  (`quizzy_player_CODE`). Clearing cookies creates a new player.
- Quiz deletion deletes its games, players and answers.
- The QR code is an inline SVG made by `rqrcode` (in the Gemfile). No CDN and no
  JavaScript library, so the app works offline.

# Quizzy: design notes

Notes for whoever builds the next release. The live game (big screen, phones) is in "Live game".
The design files live in `docs/mockups/` (style guide, quiz page, question form).

## Running it

    RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
    QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... bin/serve

`bin/serve` creates or migrates the SQLite databases (`db:prepare`), precompiles
assets (`assets:precompile`, digests into `public/assets`), and then runs Puma in
the foreground on `0.0.0.0:$PORT`. It exits with an error if one of the three
required variables is missing.

- All data lives in `storage/`: `production.sqlite3` (quizzes), `production_cache`,
  `production_queue` and `production_cable` (Solid Cache/Queue/Cable, unused so far).
- Logs go to STDOUT (default production logging). Nothing calls external services.
- Plain HTTP, no `force_ssl`, no host allow-list (`config.hosts` is empty in production).
- `GET /up` returns 200 without credentials.

## Routes and access

Everything under `/moderate` goes through `Moderate::BaseController`, which runs
HTTP Basic auth first. Unset, wrong, or empty credentials give 401 with
`WWW-Authenticate`. Unknown `/moderate/*` URLs also ask for credentials before
returning 404, so the route table does not leak to anonymous visitors.
The comparison uses `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.

| Page | Route |
| --- | --- |
| Quiz list, "New quiz" | `GET /moderate` (`moderate_root`) |
| New quiz / save | `GET /moderate/quizzes/new`, `POST /moderate/quizzes` |
| Quiz page | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id` |
| Settings (quiz form) and "Delete quiz" | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/edit`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /moderate/quizzes/:id` |
| Preview | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/preview` |
| Export (quiz as JSON in a `<pre>`) | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` |
| Import page / import (always a new quiz) | `GET /moderate/imports/new`, `POST /moderate/imports` |
| New / edit question | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/new`, `…/:id/edit` |
| Save question, delete | `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions[/:id]` |
| Move up / down | `POST /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/:id/move?direction=up|down` |
| Active checkbox | `PATCH /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/:id/activation` |

## Data model

- `Quiz`: `title` (required).
- `Question`: `quiz_id`, `text` (required), `position` (1-based, per quiz), `active`
  (default true). Inactive questions stay in the order. Numbering on the quiz page
  ("1", "2", …) counts active questions only; inactive ones show "—".
- `Option`: `question_id`, `text`, `correct`, `position`.

### Option rules (`Question`)

- Rows whose text is blank after `strip` are skipped and never saved.
- At least two filled rows: otherwise "Add at least two options".
- At least one filled row must be correct (several correct rows are fine). A
  correct box on an empty row does not count. Otherwise "Mark at least one option
  as correct".
- Validation runs on the in-memory rows. Options are only replaced after validation
  passes (`after_save`), so a rejected form leaves the database untouched. The form
  re-renders with exactly what was submitted, including empty rows and the Active box.

## Export and import (JSON)

Moderators reuse a quiz at another conference or share it with a colleague by
copying JSON. There is no file upload or download: both sides are plain text.

- **Export**: the "Export" link on the quiz page opens `/moderate/quizzes/:id/export`.
  `QuizExport` writes pretty-printed JSON into one `<pre class="code-block export-json">`
  (the only `<pre>` on the page; the CSS selects it whole on a click). The keys are
  exactly `title` and `questions`; each question has `text`, `active`, `options`; each
  option has `text`, `correct`. No ids, positions or timestamps. Inactive questions are
  exported too, and questions and options keep their order.
- **Import**: the "Import quiz" button on `/moderate` opens `/moderate/imports/new`
  with the "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button. `QuizImport` always creates
  a new quiz (titles are not matched), then redirects to its page with "Quiz imported.".
- **Optional keys**: `active` (default true) and `correct` (default false). `null`
  counts as left out. Unknown keys are ignored.
- **Types are strict**: `title`, question `text` and option `text` must be strings;
  `active` and `correct` must be true or false; `questions` and `options` must be
  lists; each question and option must be an object. A wrong shape gives one message
  such as "Questions must be a list.", with 422.
- **Rules are the form's rules**, because the same models check them: question text
  and quiz title are required; blank option rows are skipped (a correct box on a blank
  row does not count); at least two filled options; at least one correct. The messages
  are the models' messages, prefixed with the question's place in the JSON, for examp",
  "output_tail": "WS`).
- **Labels**: the row text field has a visually hidden `<label>` "Option N". The
  checkbox label reads "Option N is correct" (the visible word is just "correct",
  the context is a visually hidden prefix). Visible labels follow the design.
- **"Add option"** is a submit button (`name="add_option"`) with `formnovalidate`.
  The server re-renders the form with one more row, keeping the typed values. No
  JavaScript is needed for that.
- **Enter key**: the first submit button in the form is a hidden empty button, so
  Enter in an option field saves the question and does not trigger "Add option".
- **Active checkbox on the quiz page**: a tiny Stimulus controller
  (`auto_submit_controller.js`) calls `requestSubmit()` on change. The form has its
  own `activation` route, so it cannot touch the question text or options.
- **Confirmations** ("Delete" question, "Delete quiz") use Turbo's
  `data-turbo-confirm`, which calls the browser's native `confirm()`.
- **Redirects after POST/PATCH/DELETE** use `303 See Other`, so Turbo follows them
  with GET.
- The question and quiz forms set `data-turbo="false"` because they re-render with
  422/200 on errors and a plain form post is simpler to reason about.
- **Move up / Move down** stay enabled at the ends (the first item's "Move up" is
  dimmed with `is-edge`). A move past an end is a no-op.
- **"Add question"** and **"New quiz"** are buttons that submit a GET form to the
  new-record page, so they are `<button>`s as the brief says.
- The correct option chips on the quiz page get the design's ✓ (from CSS) and a
  visually hidden "(correct)", so screen readers hear the mark too.

## Preview: stateless by design

`QuizPreview` (app/models/quiz_preview.rb) plays the quiz using only URL parameters,
so nothing is written to the database:

- `answers=<id>,<id>,…`: option ids picked so far, one per active question, in order.
- `pick=<id>`: the option the participant just picked. The page then reveals the answer.

Flow: no params → Question 1. A pick (`GET` form button) → "Correct!"/"Wrong!", the
correct options marked, and "Next question" (or "See score" on the last question).
"Next question" carries `answers` forward. After the last answer → "Score: X/Y".
"Start over" is a plain GET to the preview URL. Answers that don't match the active
questions (for example after a deletion during the preview) redirect to the start.

Why not a Stimulus/JS state machine: the QA suite runs in a browser, but this keeps
the preview working without JavaScript and avoids storing anything. The player side
(phones) can reuse the same pattern or the same models later.

## Styling

- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` is the design's stylesheet, copied as exported.
  `Inter-latin.woff2` sits next to it. Propshaft rewrites the relative `url()` to the
  digested asset path.
- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy_app.css` holds the app-specific tweaks (option row
  grid, fieldset reset, edge state). Keep design changes out of `quizzy.css`.
- Look and feel follow the mockups: lavender page, blue ink, pink primary buttons,
  pill buttons, `.card` white panels, `.errors` pink box above the form.
- Known deviations from the mockup: no ✕ remove button on option rows (clear the
  text to drop a row, which the rules already allow); move buttons show text
  ("Move up"/"Move down") instead of arrow icons so the labels are exact.

A quiz can be played many times. "Start a game" on the quiz page creates a **game**:
its own join code, players and answers. The moderator runs it on the big screen, and
the audience joins on phones.

### Lifecycle

`lobby` (no question shown yet) -> `running` (questions open and close in turn) ->
`finished`. The moderator buttons follow the state of the current question:

| State of the current question | Big screen shows | Button |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lobby | title, join link (text), QR code, `Players: N` | Start |
| open | `Question i of n`, question, options, `Answers: x / y` | Finish |
| closed, not last | options with answer counts, `Correct` marks | Next |
| closed, last | same | End quiz |
| finished | `The quiz is over` | (none) |

- `Game`: `quiz_id`, `code` (unique), `current_position` (0 in the lobby, else the
  1-based game question on screen), `started_at`, `finished_at`, `state_version`.
- `GameQuestion` and `GameOption`: a **copy** of the quiz's active questions and options.
  Start copies them, so editing the quiz during a game does not change it. Inactive
  questions are never copied, so games skip them.
- `Player`: `game_id`, `name` (squished, at most 40 characters), `token` (random, unique).
- `Answer`: one row per player and game question (unique index). Picking again updates it.

### Transitions are guarded

`Game#start`, `#finish_question`, `#next_question` and `#end_quiz` each run an
`UPDATE ... WHERE` that matches the state the moderator saw (for example
`current_position = 2 AND finished_at IS NULL`), plus a check on the question row, all in
one transaction. A stale tab or a double click finds no matching row and is refused
with a message. `state_version` goes up on every change.

Player picks run in an immediate SQLite transaction (Rails' default for SQLite) that
checks that the question is still open. Finish takes the same lock, so no pick can land
after the close.

### Correct answers stay hidden until the close

`GameScreen#option_rows` and `PlayerScreen#option_rows` give `correct` as `nil` while the
question is open, so the markup has no way to show it. The open-question phone page
contains no "correct" text at all (checked by `test/integration/play_test.rb`, and by a
check against the production server). Signals carry no game data, so a broadcast
cannot leak either.

Phones show the result after Finish: "Correct!", "Wrong!" or "No answer", with the right
option marked "Right answer". The big screen marks correct options "Correct" after Finish.

### Live updates

- **Push**: every state change and every answer sends a short Turbo Stream
  `live_refresh` signal, with no data, to two signed streams: `[game, :screen]` (the big
  screen) and `[game, :players]` (all phones). The signal is sent after the transaction
  commits.
- **Pull**: the `live` Stimulus controller (`app/javascript/controllers/live_controller.js`)
  owns one region (`#game-screen` or `#player-screen`). On a signal, or on its timer, it
  fetches the region's HTML and swaps it in if the `data-live-version-value` changed.
  Each phone fetches its own state with its cookie, so no one sees another player's pick.
  The server answers `304` when the version has not changed (ETag).
- **Fallback**: the timer (about 3 s for the big screen, 5 s for phones, with jitter) and
  the `visibilitychange` and `online` events make a region catch up when a socket drops
  or a signal is lost. This is what copes with crowded conference Wi-Fi. Tests in
  `test/system/live_fallback_browser_test.rb` mute the push and check the timers.
- **Failed taps**: Turbo's `turbo:fetch-request-error` on a live region adds "No connection.
  Nothing was sent. Try again." The button dims while the request is in flight (`aria-busy`).
- The join form is only replaced when the quiz ends, so a name being typed is not lost.
- The custom stream action `live_refresh` is defined in `app/javascript/application.js`.

### Gotchas

- Propshaft reads `public/assets/.manifest.json` when it exists, even in test. A stale
  `public/assets` (left behind by an earlier `bin/serve`) makes the test server load an old
  `application.js`. Delete `public/assets` after a manual build, or run `bin/serve` again.
  It is gitignored.
- Turbo's broadcast assertions are not loaded into `ActiveSupport::TestCase` by default.
  `test_helper.rb` includes `Turbo::Broadcastable::TestHelper`. Use
  `assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts ..., count: 0` to assert that nothing was sent.
- A flex container splits its children into separate lines in the browser's text. A
  label and a number in separate elements inside `.counter-pill` read "Players:" and "2"
  on separate lines. Keep the label and the number in one inline element (see the
  `counter-pill` in `app/views/moderate/games/_screen.html.erb`).
- The row objects for the screens (`GameScreen::Row`, `PlayerScreen::Row`) are built
  with `correct` set to `nil` until it is revealed, so a partial cannot print a flag
  that was never revealed.

### Decisions

- A game copies the quiz when it starts, not when it is created. The lobby can wait for
  players while the moderator fixes a typo in a question. "Start a game" refuses when

# played many times: each time is a new game.
#
# Lifecycle: lobby (no question shown yet) -> running (questions open and close
# one after another) -> finished. Each change is a guarded update, so a double
# click or two moderator tabs cannot move the game twice.
#
# Starting a game copies the quiz's active questions into game_questions. The
# game plays that copy, so later edits to the quiz do not change a live game.

  CODE_LENGTH = 5
  CODE_FORMAT = /\A[#{CODE_ALPHABET.join}]{#{CODE_LENGTH}}\z/
  STALE_MESSAGE = "The game has changed. Reload the page and try again.".freeze

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :players, -> { order(:id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game

  def finished? = finished_at.present?

  def status_label

  # The game question on screen, or nil in the lobby.
  def current_game_question
    return if current_position.zero?

    game_questions.find_by(position: current_position)
  end

  def total_questions
    game_questions.count
  end

  def last_question?
    current_position == total_questions
  end

  def question_open?
    current_game_question&.open? || false
  end

  def question_closed?
    current_game_question&.closed? || false
  end

  # Moderator actions. Each returns true or false; on false, errors explain why.

  def start
    return reject("The quiz has already started.") unless lobby?
    return reject("Activate at least one question before starting the game.") unless quiz.active_questions.exists?

    transition({ started_at: nil }, { started_at: Time.current, current_position: 1 }) do
      copy_questions_from_quiz && open_game_question(1)
    end
  end

  def finish_question
    return reject(ended_message) if finished?
    return reject("Start the quiz first.") if lobby?
    return reject("No question is open.") unless question_open?

    transition({ current_position: current_position, finished_at: nil }) do
      close_game_question(current_position)
    end
  end

  def next_question
    return reject(ended_message) if finished?
    return reject("Start the quiz first.") if lobby?
    return reject("Finish the question before going on.") unless question_closed?
    return reject("This is the last question. End the quiz instead.") if last_question?

    following = current_position + 1
    transition({ current_position: current_position, finished_at: nil }, { current_position: following }) do
      open_game_question(following)
    end
  end

  def end_quiz
    return reject(ended_message) if finished?
    return reject("Start the quiz first.") if lobby?
    return reject("Finish the question before ending the quiz.") unless question_closed?
    return reject("There are more questions to show.") unless last_question?

    transition({ current_position: current_position, finished_at: nil }, { finished_at: Time.current })
  end

  # Tells the big screen to fetch its state again. Sent after the transaction has
  # committed, so the fetch sees the new state.
  def broadcast_screen_refresh
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_action_to([ self, :screen ], action: :live_refresh, target: "game-screen")
  end

  # Tells every phone in the game to fetch its own state again. Phones get their
  # personal view from their own request, so the signal carries no game data.
  def broadcast_players_refresh
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_action_to([ self, :players ], action: :live_refresh, target: "player-screen")
  end

  private

  def assign_code
    return if code.present?

    self.code = loop do
      candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.size)] }.join
      break candidate unless self.class.exists?(code: candidate)
    end
  end

  def reject(message)
    errors.add(:base, message)
    false
  end

  def ended_message
    "The quiz has ended."
  end

  # Moves the game forward only if the row still matches `conditions` (the state
  # the moderator saw). The block does the rest of the work in the same
  # transaction and returns false to undo everything.
  def transition(conditions, attributes = {})
    committed = false
    self.class.transaction(requires_new: true) do
      claimed = self.class.where(id: id, **conditions).update_all(
        attributes.merge(state_version: Arel.sql("state_version + 1"), updated_at: Time.current)

        game_question.options.create!(position: option_position, text: option.text, correct: option.correct)

    total_questions.positive?

  def open_game_question(position)
    game_questions.where(position: position, opened_at: nil).update_all(opened_at: Time.current) == 1
  end

  def close_game_question(position)
    game_questions.where(position: position, closed_at: nil).where.not(opened_at: nil)
                  .update_all(closed_at: Time.current) == 1
  end
end

# each time the screen renders.

# open, `option_rows` gives `correct` as nil, so the markup cannot leak it.
class GameScreen
  Row = Data.define(:option, :index, :count, :share, :correct)

  attr_reader :game, :join_url

  # join_url is the full link players open, e.g. http://localhost:3000/play/K7RZX.

    @join_url = join_url
  end

  # "Finish", and :finished once the quiz has ended.
  def phase
    return :finished if game.finished?
    return :lobby if game.lobby?

    question.open? ? :open : :closed
  end

  def revealed?
    phase == :closed
  end

  def question
    return @question if defined?(@question)

    @question = game.current_game_question
  end

  def position
    game.current_position
  end

  def total

  end

  def last_question?
    game.last_question?
  end

  def players_count
    game.players.count
  end

  # Players who have answered the current question (one answer each at most).
  def answers_count
    question ? question.answers.count : 0
  end

  def option_rows
    return [] unless question

    counts = revealed? ? question.answers.group(:game_option_id).count : {}
    answered = counts.values.sum

    question.options.each_with_index.map do |option, index|
      count = counts.fetch(option.id, 0)
      Row.new(
        option: option,
        index: index,
        count: count,
        share: answered.zero? ? 0 : (count * 100.0 / answered).round,
        correct: revealed? ? option.correct : nil
      )
    end
  end

  # Changes whenever what the screen shows changes. Used for ETags and as a marker in the markup.
  def version
    [ game.state_version, players_count, answers_count ].join("-")
  end

  end

    refute @game.running?

    assert_equal 0, @game.total_questions

    assert_equal "Waiting to start", @game.status_label

# The standings of a game: one entry for each player who joined, best first.
#
# Points: one for each correct answer. Speed decides ties: the total time of the
# correct answers, where each answer's time runs from the moment its question
# opened to the player's last pick. The lower total ranks higher. Players with the
# same points and the same total share a place, so the places read 1, 2, 2, 4.
#
# Computed from the database each time it is asked for. Only the finished game's
# screens and phones use it, so it is never read while players are answering.
class Leaderboard
  Entry = Data.define(:player, :place, :points, :time_us) do
    def winner? = player.winner?
  end

  attr_reader :game

  def initialize(game)
    @game = game
  end

  # Every player who joined, best first.
  def entries
    @entries ||= build_entries
  end

  def player_count
    entries.size
  end

  def entry_for(player)
    entries.find { |entry| entry.player.id == player.id }
  end

  # Players with at least one point, best first. Players with 0 points never win.
  def scoring_entries
    entries.select { |entry| entry.points.positive? }
  end

  # "Top N": the first N players of the leaderboard who have points.
  def top_winners(count)
    return [] if count < 1

    scoring_entries.first(count).map(&:player)
  end

  # "Draw": every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The rest of
  # the N prizes go at random to players with exactly the N-th place's points
  # (speed is ignored there). If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
  def drawn_winners(count)
    return [] if count < 1

    scoring = scoring_entries
    return scoring.map(&:player) if scoring.size <= count

    threshold = scoring[count - 1].points
    ahead = scoring.select { |entry| entry.points > threshold }
    tied = scoring.select { |entry| entry.points == threshold }
    (ahead + tied.sample(count - ahead.size)).map(&:player)
  end

  private

  def build_entries
    points = Hash.new(0)
    time_us = Hash.new(0)

    correct_picks.each do |player_id, picked_at, opened_at|
      points[player_id] += 1
      time_us[player_id] += ((picked_at - opened_at) * 1_000_000).round
    end

    rows = Player.where(game_id: game.id).order(:id).map do |player|
      { player: player, points: points[player.id], time_us: time_us[player.id] }
    end
    rows.sort_by! { |row| [ -row[:points], row[:time_us], row[:player].id ] }

    previous = nil
    place = 0
    rows.each.with_index(1).map do |row, rank|
      key = [ row[:points], row[:time_us] ]
      place = rank unless key == previous
      previous = key
      Entry.new(player: row[:player], place: place, points: row[:points], time_us: row[:time_us])
    end
  end

  # One row per correct pick: who picked it, when, and when the question opened.
  def correct_picks
    Answer.joins(:game_option, :game_question)
          .where(game_questions: { game_id: game.id }, game_options: { correct: true })
          .pluck(:player_id, :picked_at, "game_questions.opened_at")
          .map { |player_id, picked_at, opened_at| [ player_id, picked_at, cast_time(opened_at) ] }
  end

  def cast_time(value)
    value.is_a?(String) ? Time.zone.parse(value) : value
  end
end

# Correct answers are revealed only once the question has closed. While it is
# open, `option_rows` gives `correct` as nil, so the markup cannot leak it.
class GameScreen
  Row = Data.define(:option, :index, :count, :share, :correct)

  attr_reader :game, :join_url

  # join_url is the full link players open, e.g. http://localhost:3000/play/K7RZX.
  def initialize(game, join_url:)
    @game = game
    @join_url = join_url
  end

  # :lobby before the first question, :open while players answer, :closed after
  # "Finish", and :finished once the quiz has ended.
  def phase
    return :finished if game.finished?
    return :lobby if game.lobby?

    question.open? ? :open : :closed
  end

  def revealed?
    phase == :closed
  end

  def question
    return @question if defined?(@question)

    @question = game.current_game_question
  end

  def position
    game.current_position
  end

  def total
    @total ||= game.total_questions
  end

  def last_question?
    game.last_question?
  end

  def players_count
    game.players.count
  end

  # Players who have answered the current question (one answer each at most).
  def answers_count
    question ? question.answers.count : 0
  end

  # The standings, shown once the quiz has ended.
  def leaderboard
    @leaderboard ||= game.leaderboard
  end

  # How many prizes the moderator's "Top N" and "Draw" buttons give out.
  def prize_count
    game.quiz.winner_count
  end

  def option_rows
    return [] unless question

    counts = revealed? ? question.answers.group(:game_option_id).count : {}
    answered = counts.values.sum

    question.options.each_with_index.map do |option, index|
      count = counts.fetch(option.id, 0)
      Row.new(
        option: option,
        index: index,
        count: count,
        share: answered.zero? ? 0 : (count * 100.0 / answered).round,
        correct: revealed? ? option.correct : nil
      )
    end
  end

  # Changes whenever what the screen shows changes. Used for ETags and as a marker in the markup.
  def version
    [ game.state_version, players_count, answers_count, prize_count ].join("-")
  end
end

class PrizesBrowserTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = build_quiz(title: "Frontend Fest 2026")
    build_question(@quiz, text: "Largest planet?", options: [ [ "Jupiter", true ], [ "Mars", false ] ])
    build_question(@quiz, text: "Which protocol?", options: [ [ "WebSocket", true ], [ "FTP", false ] ])
    build_question(@quiz, text: "Which color?", options: [ [ "Blue", true ], [ "Pink", false ] ])
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}"
    click_button "Start a game"
    @code = find(".lobby__url").text[%r{/play/(\w+)\z}, 1]
  end

  def join_phone(session_name, name)
    Capybara.using_session(session_name) do
      visit "/play/#{@code}"
      fill_in "Your name", with: name
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, #{name}!"
    end
  end

  # Taps the option with this text on the phone's open question.
  def tap(session_name, text)
    Capybara.using_session(session_name) do
      click_button text
      assert_text "Your answer"
    end
  end

  test "the leaderboard, the places and the winners all arrive live" do
    join_phone(:ann, "Ann")
    join_phone(:ben, "Ben")
    join_phone(:cy, "Cy")
    join_phone(:dee, "Dee")
    assert_text "Players: 4"
    page.execute_script("window.__screenMarker = 'still here'")

    # Ann answers all three right, Ben two, Cy one, Dee none.
    click_button "Start"
    assert_text "Largest planet?"
    tap(:ann, "Jupiter")
    tap(:ben, "Jupiter")
    tap(:cy, "Jupiter")
    click_button "Finish"
    click_button "Next"

    assert_text "Which protocol?"
    tap(:ann, "WebSocket")
    tap(:ben, "WebSocket")
    click_button "Finish"
    click_button "Next"

    assert_text "Which color?"
    tap(:ann, "Blue")
    click_button "Finish"
    click_button "End quiz"

    # The big screen: one list item per player, in order.
    assert_text "The quiz is over"
    rows = all("ol.leaderboard > li.leader").map { |row| row.text }
    assert_equal 4, rows.size
    assert_match(/1\s+Ann\s+3 points/, rows[0])
    assert_match(/2\s+Ben\s+2 points/, rows[1])
    assert_match(/3\s+Cy\s+1 point\b/, rows[2])
    assert_match(/4\s+Dee\s+0 points/, rows[3])

    # The phones: each shows its place and points.
    Capybara.using_session(:ann) { assert_text "Place 1 of 4" }
    Capybara.using_session(:ben) do
      assert_text "Place 2 of 4"
      assert_text "2 points"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:dee) do
      assert_text "Place 4 of 4"
      assert_text "0 points"
    end

    # Top 3: the first three players of the leaderboard win.
    click_button "Top 3"
    assert_css "ol.leaderboard > li.leader.is-winner", count: 3
    assert_css "li.leader .leader__badge", text: "Winner", count: 3
    Capybara.using_session(:ann) { assert_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:cy) { assert_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:dee) { assert_no_text "You won!", wait: 1 }

    # Reset winners takes the marks away everywhere.
    click_button "Reset winners"
    assert_no_css "li.leader .leader__badge"
    Capybara.using_session(:ann) { assert_no_text "You won!", wait: 5 }

    # Draw: Ann and Ben are ahead of the 3rd place (Cy, with 1 point); Cy is drawn.
    click_button "Draw"
    assert_css "li.leader .leader__badge", count: 3
    assert_css "li.leader.is-winner", text: "Ben"
    assert_css "li.leader.is-winner", text: "Cy"
    assert_no_css "li.leader.is-winner", text: "Dee"
    Capybara.using_session(:cy) { assert_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:dee) { assert_no_text "You won!", wait: 1 }

    assert_equal "still here", page.evaluate_script("window.__screenMarker"), "the big screen must not reload"
  end

    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/edit"
    fill_in "Number of winners", with: "2"
    click_button "Save quiz"

    assert_text "Quiz saved."
    assert_equal 2, @quiz.reload.winner_count
  end
end

## Prizes

Once a game has ended, the moderator picks the winners on the big screen. The number of
prizes is the quiz setting "Number of winners" (`quizzes.winner_count`, default 3). Code:
`app/models/leaderboard.rb` (standings and winner rules), `Game#pick_top_winners`,
`#draw_winners`, `#reset_winners` in `app/models/game.rb`, and the finished-phase markup in
`moderate/games/_screen.html.erb` and `play/_screen.html.erb`.

### Scoring and speed

- A point is one correct answer (any correct option). A player who changes a pick is scored
  on the last pick.
- Speed breaks ties. A correct answer's time runs from `game_questions.opened_at` (set by the
  server when the question opened) to `answers.picked_at` (the player's last pick). A player's
  total is the sum over their correct answers, in integer microseconds (`time_us`), so sums
  never depend on float rounding. Wrong answers add no time. The lower total ranks higher.
- Order: points (most first), total time (least first), then join order. The join order only
  decides how tied players are listed.
- Places are competition ranks: players with the same points and total share a place, so
  the places read 1, 2, 2, 4. Players with no points share the last place.
- Everyone who joined is on the leaderboard, including players with no answers.
- Points and places are computed only after the end. During the game the phones show no
  points, and the big screen shows only answer counts.

### Winners

- **Top N**: the first N players of the leaderboard who have at least one point.
- **Draw**: the N-th entry of the scoring list gives the threshold. Players with more points
  than the threshold win. The remaining prizes are drawn at random (`Array#sample`) among the
  players with exactly the threshold's points, speed ignored. Each click draws again.
- If fewer than N players have points, all of them win. Players with 0 points never win.
- **Reset winners** clears every winner flag.
- Every pick replaces the previous winners: the flags are cleared and set in one transaction.
- Picks only work after the end. The update matches `finished_at IS NOT NULL` and bumps
  `state_version`, the same guard style as the other transitions. A pick before the end says
  "End the quiz before picking winners."
- A successful pick with nobody holding points says "Nobody has points yet, so there are no
  winners."
- N is read from the quiz each time a button is pressed, so a settings change applies to the
  next pick. `GameScreen#version` includes N, so the "Top N" label follows the setting on the
  next poll.
- Each pick sends one refresh to the big screen and one to the phones, as the other
  transitions do. The marks arrive live, with no data in the signal.

### What the screens show

- **Big screen** after End quiz: `ol.leaderboard` with one `li.leader` per player. Each
  item has the place, the name, "N points" (`pluralize`), and a "Winner" badge for winners
  (`is-winner`, from the design's leaderboard styles). The control bar gets "Top N", "Draw"
  and "Reset winners".
- **Phone** after End quiz: "Place P of T" and "N points". Winners also see "You won!"
  (`winner-banner`). A phone that never joined sees only "The quiz is over".
- The "Number of winners" field is in the quiz form, which also serves "New quiz". It has
  `min="1"`, so a browser blocks 0, and the model refuses 0 and non-integers as well.

### Export and import

The JSON export keeps its documented keys (`title`, `questions`), so it does not include the
number of winners. An import creates a quiz with the default of 3. If the number should travel
with the quiz, add it to `QuizExport` and `QuizImport` and update the key list above.

#
# Points: one for each correct answer. Speed decides ties: the total time of the
# correct answers, where each answer's time runs from the moment its question
# opened to the player's last pick. The lower total ranks higher. Players with the
# same points and the same total share a place, so the places read 1, 2, 2, 4.
#
# Computed from the database each time it is asked for. Only the finished game's
# screens and phones use it, so it is never read while players are answering.
class Leaderboard
  Entry = Data.define(:player, :place, :points, :time_us) do
    def winner? = player.winner?
  end

  attr_reader :game

  def initialize(game)
    @game = game
  end

  # Every player who joined, best first.
  def entries
    @entries ||= build_entries
  end

  def player_count
    entries.size
  end

  def entry_for(player)
    entries.find { |entry| entry.player.id == player.id }
  end

  # Players with at least one point, best first. Players with 0 points never win.
  def scoring_entries
    entries.select { |entry| entry.points.positive? }
  end

  # "Top N": the first N players of the leaderboard who have points.
  def top_winners(count)
    return [] if count < 1

    scoring_entries.first(count).map(&:player)
  end

  # "Draw": every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The rest of
  # the N prizes go at random to players with exactly the N-th place's points
  # (speed is ignored there). If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
  def drawn_winners(count)
    return [] if count < 1

    scoring = scoring_entries
    return scoring.map(&:player) if scoring.size <= count

    threshold = scoring[count - 1].points
    ahead = scoring.select { |entry| entry.points > threshold }
    tied = scoring.select { |entry| entry.points == threshold }
    (ahead + tied.sample(count - ahead.size)).map(&:player)
  end

  private

  def build_entries
    points = Hash.new(0)
    time_us = Hash.new(0)

    correct_picks.each do |player_id, picked_at, opened_at|
      points[player_id] += 1
      time_us[player_id] += ((picked_at - opened_at) * 1_000_000).round
    end

    rows = Player.where(game_id: game.id).order(:id).map do |player|
      { player: player, points: points[player.id], time_us: time_us[player.id] }
    end
    rows.sort_by! { |row| [ -row[:points], row[:time_us], row[:player].id ] }

    previous = nil
    place = 0
    rows.each.with_index(1).map do |row, rank|
      key = [ row[:points], row[:time_us] ]
      place = rank unless key == previous
      previous = key
      Entry.new(player: row[:player], place: place, points: row[:points], time_us: row[:time_us])
    end
  end

  # One row per correct pick: who picked it, when, and when the question opened.
  def correct_picks
    Answer.joins(:game_option, :game_question)
          .where(game_questions: { game_id: game.id }, game_options: { correct: true })
          .pluck(:player_id, :picked_at, "game_questions.opened_at")
  end

steps.message:
The prize feature is built on the existing game app. The full suite passes: 242 unit and integration tests and 17 browser tests, with rubocop clean. Brakeman reports only the Ruby CVE that the design notes already list as an accepted open point.

**What changed**
- **Settings:** a "Number of winners" field (number, `min` 1, default 3) on the quiz form. The model refuses 0, negatives, fractions, and blanks with messages.
- **Scoring:** a new `Leaderboard` class ranks players by points, then by the total time of their correct answers. Time runs from the question's open time to the player's last pick (`answers.picked_at`). Equal points and equal time share a place.
- **Winners:** Top N, Draw, and Reset winners. Top N takes the first N players with points. Draw keeps everyone above the N-th place's points and draws the rest at random from that tie. Players with 0 points never win. Each click replaces the previous winners. Picks are refused until the quiz has ended.
- **Big screen:** after End quiz, one `li` per player with place, name, "N points", and a "Winner" badge. The control bar gets "Top N", "Draw", and "Reset winners".
- **Phones:** after End quiz, "Place P of T", "N points", and "You won!" for winners. Nothing shows points during the game.
- **Speed:** phones now follow the moderator in about 115 to 160 ms. The live controller used to wait 150 ms before every fetch. It now fetches at once and only shares fetches inside a burst of answers.
- **Migrations:** three migrations add `quizzes.winner_count`, `players.winner`, and `answers.picked_at`. Existing answers are backfilled from `updated_at`, which I checked against pre-migration data.

**Decisions to review**
- Top N and Draw read the quiz's current "Number of winners" when pressed, so a settings change applies to the next pick. The "Top N" label follows the setting on the next poll.
- The export JSON keeps its documented keys, so the winner count is not exported. An import gets the default of 3.
- The number field has `min="1"`, so a browser blocks 0 before the server message appears. The server still refuses it.
- No confirmation dialog was added to "Reset winners" or "Draw", since the spec doesn't ask for one.

**Verification**
- `bin/serve` ran from a clean state with the required variables. `/up` returned 200, `/moderate` demanded the credentials, and the new field rendered.
- A full game ran against the production server: a settings change, a leaderboard, phone places, Top 2, Draw, and Reset. Phone updates came through the live path.

**Housekeeping**
- The design notes now have a "Prizes" section covering the rules, decisions, and latency measurement. The README has a short paragraph on prizes.
- I stopped the server and removed the databases and compiled assets I had created, so `bin/serve` will rebuild them.
- Nothing is committed. The repo's app files were untracked before I started, and I left that as it was.
